solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worry about a fine keeper of wine

indicators.note: about tells us the worry word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to worry is to care, be anxious
F is the pencil-grade and penalty abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a penalty given to the man who looks after the wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CARE around A plus F, splitting it as CAR-AF-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter-style glass jug holds and serves wine, so it is literally a container keeping it.

clue.text: Constant term woman brought up for car

parts.note: C is the standard symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to term something is to call it by a name
Ida is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A permanent word for a woman is raised in connection with a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads the term and woman words bottom to top in this down entry; 'term' is the verb, to name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cadillac is a famous American luxury make of automobile.

clue.text: Beer drunk? Number with difficulty in turn rising

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of beer are reeling about into a new order
in turn signals that the pair of following words is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: an ill is a trouble or difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone drunk on beer struggles with a number while trying to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges BEER to REBE; 'in turn' reverses NOILL to LLION. 'rising' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition, an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt against authority, the same as an armed uprising or revolt.

clue.text: Very old type ignoring ship's counter

indicators.note: ignoring means the ship letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: a fossil is an old-fashioned person, a very old type
SS is steamship, the standard abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: An ancient sort of person pays no attention to the shop counter on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart or counter it.

clue.text: Crowds right away in broadcast backing place once overseen by Smith

indicators.note: in places the shortened crowd word inside the reversed broadcast word
backing means the broadcast word is read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed from the crowds word

parts.note: hordes are crowds

explanation.surface: Crowds go missing while someone supports a broadcast about a country run by Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' and 'backing' each work on one piece, and 'in' joins them. Ian Smith led the breakaway white-minority government of the former colony.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British colony of Southern Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe, was governed by Ian Smith after his 1965 declaration of independence.

clue.text: Period inside after a drink in sporting break?

indicators.note: after places the prison-period word behind the drink word

parts.note: a half is a half pint of beer, a common British pub order
doing time is serving a period inside prison

explanation.surface: A spell in jail comes after a drink during an interval in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A half is half a pint, the usual British pub measure for a smaller drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval between the two halves of a football or rugby match is its mid-game pause.

clue.text: The deal won corruptly is shabby

indicators.note: corruptly suggests the letters of these words are twisted into a dishonest new arrangement

explanation.surface: A deal secured through bribery is a seedy business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruptly' rearranges THEDEALWON.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something run down and shabby looks worn, like shoes with worn heels.

clue.text: In it, one finds a source of heat releasing bit of sweat?

definitions.text: In it, one finds a source of heat releasing bit of sweat?

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces are placed inside the word for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it
A is one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: releasing means the bit of sweat is let go from the heat-source word

parts.note: the sun is a source of heat

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of sweat is used

explanation.surface: A hot room where you sit to sweat is described as the place a heat source releases perspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives S, which 'releasing' drops from SUN to leave UN; A plus UN goes 'In' SA. Read as a whole, the clue describes a hot room making people sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam bath or hot room is a place with a heat source where people go to perspire.

clue.text: Wise like someone who's received lessons endlessly?

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the pupil word is dropped

parts.note: a tutee is a person who is taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: Being wise is compared to someone who has been well taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, clever and perceptive, so sagacious.

clue.text: Refuse derived from river

parts.note: of can mean derived from, as in made of
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England

explanation.surface: Rubbish has come from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall. 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is waste matter or rubbish, as well as the entrails of a slaughtered animal.

clue.text: One who came out with official touring island to get information

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman who came out into society

indicators.note: touring means the official word travels around the island letter

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a sports official

explanation.surface: A debutante and an umpire travel round an island to gather facts.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'came out' into society; 'touring' puts I inside REF.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them after a mission to gather details.

clue.text: Grass cut in front of clubs, say, produces action

indicators.note: in front of places the trimmed grass word before the clubs word
cut means the grass word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass
clubs is an example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Mown grass beside golf clubs leads to a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks LAWN to LAW. 'clubs, say' looks like golf but is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case brought in court against someone.

clue.text: Flower starts to lean inside large yard

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A bloom begins to droop inside a big garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is not a container signal here; it is one of the words whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily is a well-known trumpet-shaped bloom.

clue.text: Arrange by the sound of it role lacking power in combative sport

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we want a word pronounced like the arrange word

parts.note: to marshal is to arrange in order

indicators.note: lacking means the power letter is dropped from the role word

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Organise an acting part without strength for a fighting game.
explanation.walkthrough: MARSHAL is said like MARTIAL; 'lacking' drops P from PART to leave ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate, judo and kung fu are fighting disciplines practised as a sport.

clue.text: Edward perhaps taking in northern part of Australia

indicators.note: taking in means the northern letter is placed inside the Edward phrase

parts.note: Prince Edward is a son of the late Queen, so a queen's lad

explanation.surface: Prince Edward visits the north of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Edward is the youngest son of Queen Elizabeth II, hence QUEEN'S LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Queensland is the north-eastern state of the Australian federation.

clue.text: Wrestler mostly in a round showing hostility

indicators.note: round means the whole run of preceding words is turned around
mostly means the final letter of the wrestler word is left off

parts.note: a sumo is a Japanese heavyweight wrestler

explanation.surface: A wrestler spends most of a bout displaying aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the whole run, not just the wrestler. 'in a round' looks like a boxing bout; a sumo is a Japanese wrestler.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or animosity felt toward someone.

clue.text: Oil not initially visible beside a jar

indicators.note: beside places the A after the shortened oil word
not initially visible means the first letter of the oil word is hidden from view

parts.note: camphor oil is a fragrant oil

explanation.surface: Some oil, hard to see, sits next to a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially visible' removes C from CAMPHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel.

clue.text: One notably exhibited kind temperament initially following sleep

indicators.note: following places the kind word and initial letter after the sleep word

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, the dreaming stage of sleep
a brand is a kind or type

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of temperament is used

explanation.surface: A good-natured disposition emerges after a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T from temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter's works hang in major galleries, so he is a famously exhibited artist.

clue.text: By the sound of it, annoy desperate character and bullying woman

indicators.note: By the sound of it means a word is spelt as it is pronounced, not as usual

parts.note: to harry is to annoy or harass
Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip character from The Dandy

explanation.surface: Pester a hopeless rogue and a domineering woman, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a strongman in the long-running British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a scolding, bossy old woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Rival net is broken — in which cast rests?

indicators.note: is broken suggests the letters of these words are smashed and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A competitor's net is damaged during a break in play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is the actors in a play, not a plaster cast.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval in a theatre is the pause when the actors take a break.

clue.text: Bone can keep fracturing

indicators.note: fracturing, apt for a bone, means the letters of these words break and re-form

explanation.surface: A bone can stay broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracturing' rearranges CANKEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella, the small flat bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Moralising talk excited moaners about to leave

indicators.note: excited means the remaining letters are stirred into a new order
to leave means the about letter goes out of the moaners word

parts.note: A is a dictionary abbreviation for about, used in dates

explanation.surface: Agitated complainers drop the subject in a lecture on morals.
explanation.walkthrough: A for 'about' (from Latin ante, or approximately) is less common than C or CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a lecture on duty or morals, especially a tedious one.

clue.text: Lively person's chief quality

definitions.meaning: a high-..., energetic individual, as in a free soul
the essential nature or prevailing character of something

explanation.definitionFit: A spirited person is lively, and the spirit of a thing is its essence or central character.

clue.text: Worth for all to see in servant short of time

indicators.note: in places the universal certificate letter inside the shortened servant word
short of means the time letter is missing from the servant word

parts.note: a valet is a manservant
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Merit is visible to everyone in a manservant who lacks time.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone. 'short of' takes T from VALET to give VALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Value means worth, the amount something is worth.

clue.text: Dull writer full of rambling tirades

indicators.note: full of means the writer word is filled with the rearranged letters

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: rambling suggests the letters of tirades wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tedious author keeps ranting at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' gives the anagram of the rant, which 'full of' places inside the writer word, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian prose is uninspired, ordinary and unexciting.

clue.text: Foreign magistrate once detaining duke in ruse

indicators.note: detaining means the magistrate word holds the duke letter inside it

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler holds a nobleman in a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detaining' puts D inside DOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or clever scheme to evade something.

clue.text: Woman in union taking day off for cheesy stuff

indicators.note: taking pairs with off to say a letter is taken away
off with taking means the day letter is removed from the woman word

parts.note: a bride is a woman being joined in marriage

explanation.surface: A newly married woman takes a day's leave for something cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking day off' reads like holiday leave but removes D from BRIDE. 'cheesy' hints at sentimentality but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese.

clue.text: Estonian oddly is one blowing top?

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of Estonian are taken

explanation.surface: Is an Estonian strangely someone who loses their temper?
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' sounds like temper but is a volcano erupting.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, which erupts from its summit.

clue.text: Racecourse director showing something more than caution?

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in north-east England

explanation.surface: A horse-racing director showing more than mere care.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a caution is a yellow card; the red card, sending a player off, is the step beyond it.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee shows a player this card for sending off, a harsher penalty than a booking.

clue.text: Suit worn by star, not a past actor

indicators.note: by places the shortened star word next to the rearranged suit
worn suggests the suit letters are frayed out of shape into a new order
not means the A is dropped from the star word

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A suit worn by a film star who is no longer around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' rearranges SUIT to USTI; 'not' drops A from NOVA. Peter Ustinov was a British actor, died 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Ustinov was a celebrated film and stage actor, now dead.

clue.text: Terrible gradient for walking

indicators.note: Terrible suggests the gradient letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An awful slope to walk up.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading is stepping or walking on something.

clue.text: Former president changing direction in the end for alliance

indicators.note: changing direction in the end means the final right letter is swapped for its opposite, left

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a US president

explanation.surface: An ex-president finally switches sides in a pact.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the end of CARTER becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a combination of firms colluding to fix prices, an alliance.
